Year, 30??, time and date, nobody knows for sure. Country of origin, long gone. The world or planet earth was just a planet with people randomly living in it. Or perhaps, not dying would be an accurate, unexaggerated sketch of the situation. Thirst, hunger and death were common place. The world which at maximum was able to sustain 9 billion people with a stress was now burdened with a total population of almost 23 billion, or so it is told. Though I always wondered, how did they even got that figure. It is not like there were any census or any people who would take and organize one. The world in short was literally nearing its Judgment day. People of the past speculated that Judgment might be a series of natural disasters, a sort of reset for the earth. On the other hand, the religious groups had their own beliefs. Such as the world was just a temporary rest place and Judgment would be the gate to enter the new and true life in the after. I, a boy who was given no name, asks them this, to come and watch the world from the eyes I see it daily with. It would show them what real judgement is like, when it is not a day, but days, months and years, when there is no instant death, no hope, meaning or goal and obviously no thrill of the unknown, just dread and despair. A slow, painful and time taking Judgment. It might have been planned by the God, if he so exists, but I for sure can say, we humans are the one that brought Judgement on ourselves. After all, many philosophers of the old, like Mencius who I happened to read about in a book of the old I found randomly. They claimed, human nature by default was good, and righteous. For one, he was not wrong, we humans got so wretched that we decided it is finally time to punish ourselves for what we have done, and indirectly brought the upcoming hell upon us.

“What are you writing Rig?” Juntis who whose back was pressed with mine while we were shrugged in the corner of the living room of the small one story building we were living in. I passed him the slate made of metal. A world where paper was scarce, special metal sheets were used to write on by a special type of pointer that made it apparently easy. Though I did hear, that before the Great Wars back when there used to be colonies called countries, there were devices that used electricity in the form of things called batteries to run. They despite being small were able to store thousands of information’s worth. To me it was like a fairy tale, cause after all, ‘like that’s possible.’ “Hey Rig, even if I can read that, you still do understand that I don’t get it at all. I mean what the heck. Since when did you wanted to become a History Teacher?” I couldn’t help but giggle at that thought, a teacher and me. “I just, thought of, you know, leave some last words.” “Yo Rig, you do realize that, even History Teachers don’t leave history lessons in their dying will. That would cause their families as well as to hate them, cause, the students already did you know. You got the wrong inspiration boy.” Juntis said as he burst into a laugher on his own lame joke, which was followed by my laughter, because, even if his jokes were unable to make me laugh, seeing him laugh always helped me do the trick as well.

Like the concept of courtiers was now an old thing, families were yet the same as well. People satisfied their lusts, children were born, some died, some just managed due to fate. The building, that I was living in was the same, I was born here, among the many women here, I do not know which one is my birth mother, or if she is even here. And let’s not even talk about the dads. In this small cramped place, 32 individuals live. Not like a family, but as in just live. Living place was scarce, everywhere it was a sea of people. But it was normal, because that is what my as well as everyone’s eyes opened to. People for one did not kill for living space, because be it a building, or an open ground, it was the same everywhere. For food, anything that anyone found was okay. Everyman for himself. There were times when many like me, went without a day or two, but that is normal as well, our bodies are kind of used to it. People, when found anything would be grateful and eat it without a thought, be it a corpse of a human or an animal, though animal corpse were hard to find by since they were rare. People though would not kill to eat. It was kind of strange but the concept of killing was almost none now. Perhaps it was due to common death that people did not see the point to kill anymore. Plants were also there but very few were lucky to find one. In my life, I wish I could say how many years but a world where people don’t know the date, the time, or the year, how could I have had kept a track of my own age. I never tasted what a plant was like so that day was perhaps still to come. It was the sun only which people used to plan according, it’s out, it’s day it’s gone, it’s night. Simple. Water was always a problem but the place where we lived, has this huge building which worked on its own. Situated by the sea, it gave fresh water somehow, even though it took water from the sea. It was probably something made by the people before those of the Great Wars. This sometimes makes me think whether all those Fairy Tales were actually in fact true. So we had the water problem solved. I doubt it is like that for any other place. That summarizes the life, how people live, doing nothing except living.

I put my pointer down, as well as my slade, the one I was writing on. Could not help but Yawn, and dropped down on the floor, to do what we did the most. Sleep. “Finally” Juntis said, as he dropped down alongside with me, and cuddled into me to go to his sleep. This reminded me, the cold was coming. The time when it was the most difficult to live and the time, most of the people changed around us since many died and new ones came. Who knows maybe we might get replaced by some other boys as well.

I felt someone was shaking me up. I opened my eyes, it was blurry at first but then I saw Ennis. I sat up. Juntis was still asleep. “Has Wal come back?” She nodded. Wal was our senior most in the group. We were a group of 5, friends you may call us, and Wal was the leader. It was a day when he was out for food scavenge that he found this girl and developed a weird admiration for her. It was unheard of, in this age, to stick to a person sort of making yourself their partner, it was not unheard of, but still rare. He was the second person I knew in life who did that. Due to this, Ennis, also elder than us became our 6th member.

I looked outside, the sun was still up. But I did realize, it was not the same sun, that means, during my sleep, it had gone once and came back up again. It was normal to sleep this long. Though now when Wal and Ennis were back, I presumed Hes and Sef would be arriving anytime soon. Even though we considered ourselves a group of 6, we were actually 3 pairs of 2 living and cooperating together. We would always plan our hunts in such a way that one pair would hold down the fort and look after things while the other two would go have their hunt. It was our turn to hold the front because we had our 2 hunt sessions before hand. Next it was going to be Ennis and Wal to stay back. We did not share our stuff; obviously it was still every man for himself but we did care for each other in ways. We always planned the duration of hunt in a way that, when the sun goes down, rises up again, goes down and rises up, the teams should be back by then before it can go down again. 2 times that means. Perhaps 2 days, as old people might have used this term.

It was kind of nice as well to have someone to talk to, because, even though the world was a sea of human, they hardly talked. In this building of 32 people, I only talked to 7 of them, the rest, one hardly cared or even remembered whether they were here before or someone new. I was still looking at Ennis wondering what to talk to her, because, she for one could not talk. For some reason her ability to talk never devolved. It would hardly have been a problem normally since people did not talked either ways, but, at situations like these, I would think, it would be good to hear a word or two, and plus she herself might wasn’t to speak as well, if not to me, at least to Wal who cared so much for her. Short shaggy hair that reached her shoulders, stiff and kind of fuzzed, I’m sure they would be longer if she combed them properly. With a bit of dirt on her face that was common everywhere, she had freckles and a round cute face with eyes that were more alive than any others I had seen. It was her eyes she used the most to talk with after all. Green rags that went from her shoulder to thighs, she was a normal nice girl.

After coming up with nothing to say, she looked at Juntis and then back at me, signaling me to wake him up as well. “Did Wal asked you to wake us up?” she nodded yet again. I looked at the pointer that was still laying where I had slept. I looked back at Ennis and a weird smile took over my face. I picked it up, and with a flash pinch Juntis in the ribs who with a shock and lightening movements suddenly jumped up and crashed against the wall. Now this time, I could not help but laugh, even Ennis smiled as if to enjoy that reaction. Juntis who was still dazed and not sure what happened was staring at us as if we were the void and then suddenly got up and smacked me on my back, in a friendly manner but it hurt a lot. He was elder and bigger than me, the second eldest after Wal, but biggest in size, kind of chubby but not fat, tall and dark toned, wearing glasses that had no lenses, for he kind of liked his face more with glasses. He had a small rough beard that was probably going to grow bigger with time if not dealt with. And his short spiky hairs were kind of always a fun feeling to feel while rubbing his round head. Seeing Ennis, he realized Wal was back. “Have Hef and Sef come back as well?” “I don’t know” I told him while Ennis shook her head in negation as well. “Finally time to go out.” Juntis was excited. He enjoyed going out. And it was because of people like him, and the rest of the group, that even though, we all considered it Judgment time, it was still adventurous in our own way. Though seeing others around me, it was not the case for them so I did consider myself to be the luckier one even in these situations. Plus, being the youngest, it’s always nice to have people to look on.

The main door opened, and we saw Wal, tall and thin but well built, with sharp looking face features and long golden hair though dirtied with mud, reaching his neck. He was wearing a white vest from which his thin but shaped up arms were visible and as usual his serious expression which made him look as if he was angry all the times even though he was not, was still adorned his face. Seeing him made us kind of happy. Following him were Hef and Sef, non-identical twins who have supported each other from long before we became a group. They too joined us from the outside and later started living with us, only because some people who used to lodge besides us one day just never came back. It was me, Juntis and Wal who met both of them in the past one day when we were out drawing water. Juntis was also born in this building, though he did know who his mom was, he never cared. Whereas Wal was a similar case like me. Hef was a weak, dark complexioned, small heighted kid but with clever wits and a smart brain. It was always beneficial for us to have him. Sef was in comparison healthier and fair in complexion, about the same height as Hef who was a bit taller than me. Sef was physically weak and the only talent he had was his memory. He could always remember ways and texts etc very well. This made him a pretty good guide for when outside and in search of the way back. Both the brothers had soft looking faces making them look a bit naïve but the reality was far from it. In times like these, even the youngest like me with no definite skills except better writing and reading ability was on my wits all the times because anything can happen at any time. All 5 except Ennis had proper clothing since Hef and Sef once found some for us, but back then Ennis was not with us. Plus, it was only enough for us to have either way. Clothing was the least of worries but we knew Wal wanted her to have proper cloths as well and he was trying. The cloths he found on corpses were always no better so all he could do was wait.

With the band together. It was time for us to go out. We were to go and get water while Hef and Sef would be on the food hunt. Leaving Wal and Ennis behind, we made our way.

“You get the bag; I will wait outside.” I told Juntis while heading out. The building was on the front most street, which was a good thing. Though, ahead spread a wide number of people. As if some exhibition was going on, or something from the space has landed. Our area was quite better than many other lands, so the people opting for here are more, but this calls for competition. Before even reaching here, more than half are killed in fighting. Another common thing here were sects. It was not uncommon now to see people appearing claiming to be messengers from god and promises of salvation. Being a kid, even I can distinct the fact that it’s a scam but a huge number of people are still part of their idiocy. They must be desperate too I guess, for ways to calm down, and have a peaceful end. For one thing I always observed. Religious people true to their teachings, whether true or false, it does not matter, are at peace. And like always, sights such as these were common in the center points. “Come on, let us go.” Juntis said as he moved out without caring a thing for the scenery. Though it is not as if I cared for it, it was just pitiable but, I wonder if ii have the right to pity them.

Dusty, cloudy brownish blue sky, yet the sun shining clearly, hitting everyone with it arrows of light. No matter how use to you get, it still burns and stings. The broken ground with cracks, devoid of all green, hot as it already was, enough to make your shoes stick to it. The time of cold was coming near, but the day always hits hot. Even then, when it is cold, and the body temperatures are down, the ground and the sun keeps on reminding you, that heat is not going to lose the cold. This is quite the vulnerable time, most kids usually die during this period due to sickness, which was common as births of new babies. Even Wal don’t let me go outside much during those days, and that is the cooperation we get that I talked about. Walking our way, we kept walking, closer the sea, where its cooler but one still sweats a lot. It was right about then, when I saw the person, the only person that I did not want to see.
